topic: California petition for change of name
statement: In California you change your legal name by filing papers in court. If a judge agrees, you get a court order that states your new legal name, and you use that order to change your name on your identity documents.
detail: You pay a filing fee of $435 to $450. If you cannot afford it, you can ask the court to waive it. Before a judge can decide, your forms must be published in a newspaper for one month. But you do not have to publish if your name change is to match your gender identity, or if you file it with a request for gender change recognition. A judge makes a decision in about 2 to 3 months.

cost.note: The filing fee is $435 to $450. If you cannot afford it, you can ask the court to waive it. Publishing in a newspaper has its own fee, which the guide does not state.

timeline.typical: a judge makes a decision in about 2 to 3 months

source.title: California Courts Self-Help — Change Your Name

topic: California name-change form for a gender-identity name change
statement: To change your name for reasons related to gender identity, California uses form NC-200, the Petition for Change of Name to Conform to Gender Identity. You use it to start a case to change your name, or your minor child's name.
detail: The Judicial Council lists form NC-200 as the petition that starts this kind of case. The courts also publish how-to instructions and form packets for a name change and for a gender change.

source.title: California Courts — Petition for Change of Name to Conform to Gender Identity (NC-200)

topic: California petition for change of gender
statement: California lets you petition for a court recognition of a change of gender and sex identifier, and you can request a name change in the same set of forms.
detail: You do not need to give any medical documentation to get a court order recognizing a gender change, or to change California state-issued documents. You can ask for a gender marker of female, male, or nonbinary.

cost.note: The filing fee is $435–$450. If you cannot afford it, you can ask the court to waive it.

timeline.typical: about two months; a judge decides in about 1 to 2 months

source.title: California Courts Self-Help — Change Your Legal Gender

statement: To change the name on your California driver's license or ID, first change your name with the Social Security Administration. Then use the DMV's online application to apply for a new DL/ID card with your new name. Your name change is not complete until you come into a DMV field office.
detail: The DMV checks your information with Social Security first. If the two do not match, your application is denied. Bring proof of your true full name from the DMV's acceptable documents list. If you have legally changed your name before, the DMV may also ask for a name change document that shows your legal name both before and after the change.

cost.note: The page does not state an amount. It says to be ready to pay the appropriate licensing fee.

source.title: California DMV — Update Information on Your Driver's License or ID Card

statement: California lets you pick a gender category of male (M), female (F), or nonbinary (X) on your driver's license or ID card. You use the DMV's online application to apply for a new card with the updated gender category.
detail: The DMV says your gender category change is not complete until you come into a field office. The DMV page no longer names a paper Gender Category Request form; it routes the change through the online DL/ID application instead. Be ready to pay the appropriate licensing fee.

cost.note: The DMV page does not list a separate gender-category fee. It says to be ready to pay the appropriate licensing fee.

timeline.typical: not complete until you visit a DMV field office

source.title: California DMV — Update Information on Your Driver's License or ID Card

statement: If you were born in California, you can change the sex field on your birth record to reflect your gender identity by mailing in form VS 24B, the Application to Amend a Birth Record.
detail: California Vital Records takes all birth amendment requests by mail. The amendment page does not state a fee or a processing time. It links to the current fee page and the current processing-time page instead.

source.title: California Department of Public Health — Amending a California Birth Record

topic: California birth certificate: no court order needed
statement: In California you can change the gender marker or sex identifier on a birth certificate without a court order and without medical certification.
detail: The state courts' self-help guide says to update (amend) your California birth certificate through the California Department of Public Health.

source.title: California Courts Self-Help — Update your gender marker or sex identifier on your identity documents

statement: To change the name on a California birth record after a court order, mail in form VS 23, the Application to Amend a Birth Certificate After a Court Order Name Change.
detail: You need the signed court order first. California Vital Records takes all birth amendment requests by mail, and it will ask you for more paperwork if your request is short of what it needs.

source.title: California Department of Public Health — Amending a California Birth Record

statement: California's fee list shows a $26 fee to amend a birth record. It covers a court-order name change (form VS 23) and a change to the sex field, and it includes one free copy of the new record.
detail: The fee to change or correct the sex field is $26 no matter when you ask for it. Extra certified copies of a California birth record cost $31 each. Pay by check or money order, not cash.

cost.note: Includes one free copy of the amended record. Extra certified copies are $31 each.

source.title: California Department of Public Health — Vital Records Fees

topic: California name change for a minor child
statement: In California, a parent, guardian, or near relative can ask a court to change a minor child's name. The California Courts self-help guide says the forms and steps for a child's name change are different from an adult's.
detail: If you are a parent filing to change your child's name without the other parent, you must serve (officially deliver) that other parent a copy of the forms. The guide does not say the other parent must agree to the name change, only that they must be served with notice of it. A name change does not change who a child's legal parent is: changing a child's name does not add anyone to the birth certificate or grant legal parentage. Before a judge can decide, the request must usually be published in a newspaper for one month, but the guide says you do not have to publish if the name change is to match gender identity or is filed together with a request for gender change recognition — the guide states this exception for name changes in general, not only for adults. The guide does not name an age at which the child's own consent or objection is required, and its instructions do not use a "best interest of the child" standard.

cost.note: The guide states the same $435 to $450 filing fee for name changes in general, with a waiver available if you cannot afford it. It does not name a separate fee for a child's case.

source.title: California Courts Self-Help — Change Your Name

topic: California petition to recognize a minor child's gender change
statement: In California, a parent or guardian can ask a court for an order recognizing their child's gender change, and can ask for a name change in the same forms. The guide says a child does not need to have had any gender-affirming care to get this order, and no medical documentation is required.
detail: If you are a parent asking for a court order recognizing your child's gender change without the other parent, you may have to serve (officially deliver) the other parent a copy of the forms. The guide does not say the other parent must agree, only that they must be served with notice of the case. The guide does not name an age at which the child's own consent or objection is required, and its instructions do not use a "best interest of the child" standard.

cost.note: The guide states the same $435 to $450 filing fee for this court order. If none of the parents can afford the fee, they can ask the court to waive it.

source.title: California Courts Self-Help — Change Your Legal Gender

topic: California birth certificate sex field for a minor child
statement: California's Assembly Bill 218 lets a parent or guardian get an amendment to a birth certificate for their minor or adult child to reflect the child's gender identity. Since January 1, 2023, this process does not require a court order if the family sends in the required supporting documentation.
detail: The same form used for an adult, VS 24B (Application to Amend a Birth Record), also covers changing the sex field on a child's birth certificate and updating a parent's own designation to reflect the parent's gender identity.

source.title: California Department of Public Health — Assembly Bill (AB) 218
